sections.heading: Gain <= 1 limitation
sections.text: The SRC (series resonant converter) has a maximum voltage gain of 1 — it cannot step up the voltage. If the output cannot reach the target, verify the turns ratio is sufficient. The SRC is fundamentally limited to V_out <= V_in*N_sec/N_pri.

sections.heading: Light-load regulation loss
sections.text: At very light load, the SRC gain curve becomes extremely flat near resonance. The converter cannot regulate because large frequency changes produce negligible output change. This is a fundamental SRC limitation — consider LLC or LCC which have better light-load regulation.

sections.heading: Subharmonic oscillation
sections.text: If the SRC shows oscillation at sub-harmonics of the switching frequency, the operating point may have jumped to the capacitive side (below resonance). Ensure the control always operates on the inductive side (f > f_r) for ZVS and stability.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the SRC cannot regulate across the required load range, upgrade to LLC (adds parallel inductor for better gain range) or LCC (adds parallel capacitor for high-voltage applications). The SRC is best suited for applications with narrow load range and V_out < V_in*N.
